rationale: This is essentially a one-variable substitution inside the archive's strongest signal (che/act → (che−dlc)/act) that mechanically grafts on the already-tested Net-Liquid Profitability leg, so it is a cosmetic refinement with limited incremental information, and netting dlc also destroys the bounded "floor" interpretation the original relied on.

The second leg, NEG(Δwcap/lagged assets), is a direct restatement of the published working-capital accruals anomaly, and multiplying it by a profitability-change rank is the standard textbook "earnings quality" screen already partially covered by the archive's Working-Capital Harvest, so novelty is minimal.

The liquidity leg is a genuinely different construct from the archived cash/current-asset floor — cash coverage of non-debt (operating accrual) current liabilities, bounded and well-behaved — and the MIN bottleneck matches the stated "profit backed by settlement capacity" mechanism with consistent sign.

The expression computes what the hypothesis states, but subtracting dpc from oancf mostly loads on capital/depreciation intensity rather than cash-earnings quality, and pairing it with oiadp (already net of depreciation) double-penalizes the same item while sitting close to the published cash-based operating profitability result.

Applying 3-year moving averages to both legs of the archived Debt-Interest Timing Gap is a smoothing-parameter variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the averaged Δdlc term telescopes into multi-year debt growth, pulling the signal toward the known debt-issuance/asset-growth anomaly.

Revenue-scaled noncash-current-asset intensity measured as a multi-year trend is a distinct construct from the archive's asset-scaled one-period accrual changes, the MIN bottleneck cleanly encodes "sustained margin requiring less accrual capital," and the sign direction is internally consistent.
